_unit: Year-round — the exam's own task words
_activity: General Reading Vocabulary — Regents task words
_licence: Transcribed, not invented — from US11R_Glossary_v2_2026-09-02, Tier A. Several are NYSED's own printed exam definitions (cause, effect). Reusable year-round, not unit-bound.

items.definition: What was already happening when the document was created. Asked directly on both SEQ sets.
hints: Think about timing — what's already going on.
It's the situation surrounding the document, before the document itself happened.

items.definition: Something that contributes to the occurrence of an event. NYSED prints this definition on the exam.
hints: This is the 'why' side of a cause-effect pair.
NYSED's own printed definition: something that contributes to an event happening.

items.definition: What happens as a consequence. NYSED prints this definition on the exam.
hints: This is the 'what happened next' side.
NYSED's own printed definition: what happens as a consequence.

items.definition: A major event, idea, or development that brings about significant change.
hints: Think big and lasting, not small and temporary.
An event or idea that brings about significant, lasting change.

items.definition: How two documents line up or diverge. One of the three SEQ Set 1 relationships.
hints: This is about comparing two documents to each other.
How they line up, or how they diverge — one of the three SEQ Set 1 relationships.

items.term: audience / purpose / bias / point of view
items.definition: The four reliability angles SEQ Set 2 asks about one named document.
hints: These four all ask about the reliability of a single source.
Who made it, for whom, why, and from what angle — the SEQ Set 2 angles.

items.definition: Name it. No explanation required — but naming it is required.
hints: This is the lightest-lift task word — no reasoning required.
Just name it correctly — that's the whole task.

items.definition: Say what it was, with enough detail that someone who wasn't there could picture it.
hints: This one wants detail, not reasoning.
Enough detail that someone who wasn't there could picture it — but no 'because' required.

items.definition: Say why or how. If your sentence has no "because," "which shows," or "this proves," you probably described instead.
hints: This is the task word that demands reasoning, not just detail.
If your sentence doesn't have 'because,' 'which shows,' or 'this proves,' you're probably still describing.

_hint_model: 2 escalating hints per item, available during the regular season only. Playoffs run cold (no hints), per BK's ruling 2026-09-22.
